articleTitle: Towards a more comprehensive approach to hydro-thermal power system scheduling by Lagrangian relaxation
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: It has been shown that a practically sized hydro-thermal power system, such as the Scottish system can be modelled comprehensively, and the associated short-term scheduling problem solved within reasonable time-scales, using Lagrangian relaxation techniques. This method allows the hydro-thermal scheduling problem to be split into the separate scheduling of individual thermal units and hydro-system river valleys, co-ordination between these sub-problems being achieved by iteratively updating a set of numbers known as Lagrange multipliers, until the optimum is found.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Real time simulation of power system transient behaviour
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: A power system consisting of generating plant and transmission lines is a high order nonlinear dynamic system. Many factors affect its ability to return to some normal operating point following a disturbance. The response of a disturbed power system ranges from fast electromagnetic transients, through electromechanical power swings, to slower modes influenced by the prime mover boiler and fuel feed systems. The authors discuss the simulation of the electromechanical transients caused by disturbances such as network faults and/or plant outages. System states must be evaluated at intervals of the order of tens of milliseconds over timescales of several seconds.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Calculational fault location for electrical distribution networks
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The authors discuss the theoretical basis and implementation of calculational fault location for radially operated electrical distribution networks. The integration of fault location into other control systems of the networks are also considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A review of automatic contingency selection algorithms for online security analysis
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: An essential aspect of modern power system security assessment is the consideration of any contingencies which may arise due, for example, to planned or unplanned outages of lines, and which may cause system overloads. For power systems comprising of several hundred lines, it is impractical to examine all possible contingencies. Therefore, the system engineer makes a judgement, based on intuition and experience, and ranks contingencies in order of importance. An automatic contingency selection algorithm can assist this process of security assessment by providing an objective criterion to select the most critical contingencies in a given system state and to limit the number of contingencies included in this assessment. The author presents a critical assessment of automatic contingency selection methods as reported in the literature, and identifies the general requirements of automatic contingency selection algorithms in the real-time monitoring and control of power systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Secure automatic generation control. Principle, simulation models and results
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: Electricity de France is now developing new tools for power system monitoring and control, so-called 'CASOAR' program, with new national and regional control centres new data transmission equipment and new power plant control systems. This will be achieved in several stages, leading to a more and more integrated and automatic control of the power system. The first stage will improve real time knowledge of the system state, with new analysis and decision aid tools. Then, daily power planning updating during the day will be achieved. Then, using the results of the previous stages, a new closed loop secure automatic generation control (AGC) will be implemented. The authors describe the development state of this closed loop secure AGC, including the basic concepts; the scheduled software organization, a description of the simulation models built up and used in the development process, and the results obtained so far.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dynamic power system simulation for real time dispatcher training
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The simulation of the power system is one of the basic tasks of the dispatcher training simulator (DTS). It enables responses to the trainee's actions in a manner consistent with the power system operation. The authors briefly outline the structure of a training simulator and then concentrate on the modeling of the power system. The following models are provided to simulate the dynamics of the power system and the data acquisition; turbine and governor model; boiler model; generator model; load model; frequency calculation model; relay model; voltage regulator model; network model; and telemetry model.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Object oriented techniques in an energy management system
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The authors describe a technique used to apply object oriented programming (OOP) to the design of an integrated energy management system (IEMS) by the Power Research Group at the University of Calgary. The architecture of the IEMS is briefly outlined. Each component of the system is then discussed in more detail with attention being placed on the potential for exploitation of OOP technology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementation of an AGC-algorithm in different power systems and on different control levels
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The scheduling and control of power generation are vital aspects in the daily operation of power systems. Their overall objective is to control the electrical power output generated so as to supply ever changing customer demand for power as economically as possible. An automatic generation control (AGC) program operating within a computer control centre can provide the necessary means to the dispatchers to perform this continuous task. The authors present an overview of the functional requirements for generation control software, and design principles enabling flexibility and easy maintenance when integrating such a closed loop, time critical function into a control system. Operating philosophies used in various countries to which ABB has supplied VAX based EMS systems, and how the basic AGC software package is used to satisfy the required criteria, are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A parallel computation of state estimation by transputer (poor systems)
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: It is important for the secure operation of a power system to grasp its operating conditions on-line. The authors develop a parallel state estimation program using an MIMD computer which consists of four transputers and apply it to the test systems. The key idea of the proposed method is that the gain matrix is transformed into a bordered block diagonal matrix by using a network partitioning procedure based on the factorization path. The parallel program is 30% faster in execution time compared with the serial program.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Visual aids for substation monitoring and security control
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: Imatran Voima Oy owns 70% of the high-voltage (110-400 kV) network in Finland. The control of the network, substations and power plants is carried out via the System Control Centre in Vantaa and seven District Control Centres. All substations are unmanned, controlled by SCADA-systems and equipped with fire and intruder alarm systems. In the case of a fault or accident, a large amount of information is transferred to the control room. From this information it is very often difficult to make quick conclusions and decisions of present situation and how the situation is developing. One way of increasing the preparedness and efficiency in fault and emergency situations is to use remote video surveillance systems. A live picture from the unmanned substation is considered to be of great help in the security control and in certain operation tasks. The author describes the video surveillance system and its operation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Long term simulation of the Israel power system dynamic response a case study
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: Long term simulation of the dynamic response of power systems has received much attention for several years. However, there are still numerous difficulties involved in reconstructing widespread disturbances. The authors describe the experience gained at the Israel Electric Corporation (IEC) using long term simulation for the reconstruction of a system wide contingency for a period of 15 minutes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An expert system approach for auscultation of distribution systems
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: In line with its quality of supply enhancement policy, Electricite de France (EDF) has developed and tested a monitoring and maintenance method for a medium voltage network. The method is referred to as 'auscultation' and involves, close analysis of medium voltage overhead line feeders in order to detect weak points and thereby improve targeting of maintenance and renewal operations. Auscultation was first tested on a set of ten representative networks between 1984 and 1987. The method improved EDF's knowledge of how supply systems degrade and the ensuing improvements in quality of supply were better than expected. Auscultation is only effective if it is carried out systematically and extremely rigorously, and it quickly became obvious that computerization would be a valuable asset for those responsible for analyzing data on these incidents. EDF's Research and development division therefore defined and developed a prototype expert system, which is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Inter-substation data communications for the revitalisation of network protection and control
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: In established cable distribution networks, it is rare that digital communication systems will have been installed. The revitalisation of these networks' protection and control systems by the installation of a totally new digital communications media can be prohibitively expensive. The authors introduce research into the use of existing copper circuits for inter-substation digital data communications. Available circuits consist of either protection pilots used for unit relaying schemes or the energised power conductors themselves where pilots are not available.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distribution control centers-extending system operational capabilities
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The authors look at power system distribution control centres which use distribution supervisory control and data acquisition (DSCADA) systems. DSCADA is proving to be a very useful tool in power system operation. Dispatcher remote control of substation and feeder equipment is performed routinely. Feeder re-configuration through control of sectionalizing switches for both maintenance and load switching has proven to be a valuable asset.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Interactive power restoration simulator using a microcomputer
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The authors present a package using microcomputer with full graphic features to simulate supply interruption in a typical distribution network to train operation personnel for speedy power restoration. Simulated faults can be generated randomly by the software program or applied by the user, to either the bus side or circuit side of a particular feeder in the network. The package has subprograms to calculate and display the fault current distribution, the line flows and to simulate operation of overcurrent relays responding to the fault. As a training tool, the simulator provides 'pause' facility to allow the user to fully acknowledge the operating conditions, or to be sure of his intermediate response before entering into the next scene of the supply interruption simulation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimal design of measurement points for power system state estimation
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: Power system state estimation is the process of estimating, from real time measurement data, the network power flows and busbar voltages. The authors analyse the relation between the total variance of state estimation errors and the locations of measurement points, and the parameters of the network. It is found that the total variance of the state estimation errors differ significantly when the same given number of measurements are placed at different locations in the network. The method utilises an optimal measurement tree which minimised the total variance of the state estimation errors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distribution management systems
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: London Electricity prepared a functional specification and placed an order for a control room graphics and information system (CRGIS) in 1988 which is now installed in London. The aim of the system is to replace the existing large wall diagrams with high resolution graphic displays coupled with an online computer database containing the current operational state of the distribution network. CRGIS presents to the control engineers colour diagrams of the London Electricity distribution network, full pan and zoom facilities, automatic diagram dressing, document generation facilities and access to plant information. The system database contains information relating to some eleven thousand five hundred substations, the plant contained within them and the cables connecting them.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Low-cost under-frequency relay for distributed load shedding
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: An under-frequency load shedding relay utilizing a single-chip microcomputer is described. The device may be used to shed off-peak load, thus replacing expensive emergency reserve over the corresponding periods. Economic analysis shows that the device is cost-effective when controlling loads with an installed capacity greater than about 20 kW. Use of an existing contactor, associated with a radio teleswitch for example, would reduce the cost of the relay and further improve the economic case for this application. The savings which accrue from the proposed approach increase with the installed capacity of the controlled load. Application to a limited number of large off-peak installations could replace a significant amount of emergency reserve in an isolated supply system at modest cost.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Data management for the monitoring and analysis diagnosis assistance system
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: In order to minimize maintenance and outage costs, Electricite de France is extending the existing data processing chains towards computer-aided interpretation and diagnosis. EDF is currently designing an integrated monitoring and diagnosis assistance system, PSAD (Poste de Surveillance et d'Aide au Diagnostic). PSAD is devoted to on line monitoring and diagnosis of the main components of nuclear power stations such as reactor coolant pumps, turbine generator, and primary circuit. The authors present the objectives and the functional decomposition of PSAD, and deal with the data management part of PSAD which is the center of the system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Online algorithms for the avoidance of voltage collapse: reactive power management and voltage collapse margin assessment
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The authors propose two algorithms for online application which would provide advice to the power system control engineer for the avoidance of voltage collapse. The first algorithm is Reactive Power Management (RPM) which recommends targets for despatch to generating plant, targets for the local control systems of compensation plant, and any manual switching of shunt capacitors and reactors. The second algorithm assesses the margin of a power system from voltage collapse under the existing reactive targets. It expresses the voltage collapse margin (VCM) as the additional active power transfer which could be sustained over defined geographical boundaries. Both algorithms take into account the conditions which would result from defined contingencies, as well as the prevailing intact network conditions. VCM advises on limitations which need to be placed on active power despatch to maintain system security, and RPM recommends action which would help avoid these limitations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Transient stability assessment of a turbine generator using state estimation and optimal feedback. A neural network approach
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: A back propagation artificial neural network is used to assess the transient stability assessment of a turbine generator equipped with a governor, voltage regulator and digital power system stabiliser. The ability to learn, interpolate and reproduce behaviour is presented, showing how the stability of a high order nonlinear system can be obtained without the prior solution of the state equations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A fuzzy logic based self-tuned power system stabilizer
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The application of a self-tuned fuzzy controller as a power system stabilizer is introduced. The output stabilizing signal from the controller is computed using a standard fuzzy membership function as well as a self tuning parameter. The calculation is based on the representation of the alternator state in the phase plane. Simulation results have been performed for various operating conditions under different disturbances. The results demonstrate the effectiveness and improved response of the proposed controller. It does not require any parameter identification in real time and has a much simpler algorithm than that for a self-tuning controller which is based on the adaptive control technique.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementation of state estimator and security assessor software on the Scottish hydro-electric 275 kV system
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The authors describe the initial test results of the implementation of state estimator and security assessor software on the Scottish hydro-electric 275 kV system. A brief outline of the underlying theory of the state estimator and security assessor is given, and online test results from the state estimator, including bad data replacement, and security assessor are presented. The background associated with the combined algorithm implementation and also the problems encountered with the estimator convergence are discussed and finally the estimator results of a continuous 24-hour run undertaken at the control centre are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Planning installation and operation of a hydro-generation control centre
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: Scottish Hydro Electric PLC is responsible for the generation, transmission and distribution of electricity over an area of 55167 square kilometres situated north and west of a line from the Firth of Tay to the Firth of Clyde. 55 hydroelectric stations are located throughout this area and 47 of the major stations are operated and administered from two control centres situated north and south of the Grampian mountain range. The authors describe the plant that is controlled, planning of the control system and control centres, the instrumentation and control equipment, and operational experience.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design and implementation of Ontario Hydro's new energy management system
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The responsibility for the integrated operation of Ontario Hydro's Bulk Electric System (BES) rests with the System Control Centre (SCC). In 1985, because of concerns relating to equipment obsolescence, space restrictions and site security, Ontario Hydro decided to build a new SCC located in Clarkson some 30 km west of Toronto. It became operational on schedule in December 1990. The author provides an overview of the high level user requirements for the new SCC, focusing on the data acquisition and computer system and the resulting impact that the user requirements had on the computer architecture for this energy management system. The author also provides a brief outline of the commissioning processes and operational experience during the first two months of operation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Numerical control in HV/MV substations-EDF considerations
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: Electricite de France wished to examine the developments necessary for the control of MV installations in substations. The authors look at the existing situation including costs and substation equipment renewal. It is concluded that the protection and control system of virtually all existing substations should be modified within the next 12 years. The development of a new numerical control system around a LAN is envisaged.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The evolution of distribution network management systems
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The author describes the evolution and application of network management systems (NMS) which are enabling electrical utilities to improve the efficiency of their subtransmission and distribution operations. Such a system brings great flexibility to operations and it will integrate with work management and facility management systems. Integration with customer services will improve the responsiveness of a utility to its clients. The active network topology provides a platform for advanced control techniques, improvement of security and contingency planning and systems to assist in switching plans and control decisions. The NMS system will form a cornerstone in the development of automatic restoration capabilities. NMS are a cost effective distribution control application.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integrated substation measurement, data acquisition and communications
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: An integrated system providing the features of both expanded measurement and data capture coupled with local processing can be of significant benefit to the utility. This type of integrated system is a cost-effective means of providing enhanced data flow within the utility, allowing utility personnel to obtain a detailed profile of the distribution system and to implement cost-saving procedures. The authors describe the design of such an integrated substation measurement and data acquisition system, as well as demonstrate how this integrated approach can improve the data flow within the utility. More precise measurement information can give a clearer picture of power system performance and ultimately help attain improved efficiency.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Some unusual application functions (power system computer control)
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The latest generation of digital computer-based control systems has enabled basic SCADA functions to be complemented by extensive data processing and graphic display facilities. The more advanced control systems also include energy management systems (EMS) to optimise power network operation and power system application (PSA) software to improve network security. The authors discuss some applications using hard-wired logic which have not been fully exploited on computer-based systems. Other application functions have taken advantage of digital computer processing and a number of these, which do not fall under commonly met EMS or PSA functions, are also described. The unusual functions have been specially developed to suit particular power network requirements and interface with basic SCADA functions. The authors also describe the basic functions of these applications and outline the principal features of the hardware and software to implement the functions. Experience gained from the operation of the applications is also described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Microprocessors in substation control
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: As part of the management of the National Grid, the Information Technology Department of National Grid (NGC-IT) is developing a suite of systems to enable National Grid substations to be brought under microprocessor control. The authors examine developments in three major control areas, automatic voltage control (AVC), automatic reactive switching (ARS) and computerised auto-switching (CAS), in some detail and discuss the quality standards achieved by the developments. The authors believe that the installation of microprocessor controllers can lead to substantial savings in manpower costs whilst maintaining the high standards of reliability of the Grid that the public has the right to expect.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of optimal emergency control strategies for Abu Dhabi power system
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The isolated power system for Abu Dhabi, UAE, consists of 200 kV, 132 kV and 33 kV transmission network, supplying the 11 kV and 415 volts distribution substations. This power was generated by a mixture of gas turbine (30-40% of spinning machines) and steam turbines of various capacities ranging from 15 MW to 160 MW. At low or medium load condition the largest unit (160 MW) or even the next largest unit (85 MW) can constitute about 15% to 20% of the spinning generators. Therefore, in the absence of proper emergency control strategies, the trip of a large unit can cause the system frequency to fall below the acceptable levels, and endangers the system operation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A standards based energy management system architecture providing open connectivity, open ended expansion and incremental upgradability
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The authors describe a unique energy management System architecture which is based on industry standards and the objective of insuring extensibility and upgradability to meet the new requirements imposed by electric power utilities. It is a distributed network architecture which is predicated on local area network (LAN) topology and the application of formal and widely used de facto industry standards. This unique architecture provides a solid and highly portable platform for continuous upgradability which is inherently extensible without practical limit.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A real time expert system for fault diagnosis on a transmission network
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The authors present AHFA, a real-time expert system which interprets simultaneous faults on the National Grid Company power system. It includes on object oriented graphical user interface to simplify entering the system specific knowledge. Tests so far with real and simulated data have shown AHFA to meet its goal and to be faster and more powerful than similar expert system elsewhere.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Innovative aspects of ESB's distribution SCADA scheme
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The Electricity Supply Board (ESB), Ireland, is the statutory body entrusted with the generation, transmission, distribution and sale of electricity within the Republic of Ireland. The authors provide a brief description of ESB's distribution SCADA project with an emphasis on some of its more unusual aspects.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A method to monitor transient security in optimal power dispatch
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: A method to include on-line dynamic security assessment in optimum dispatch operation of power system is presented. This methodology possesses a number of innovative features. First, the formulation extends the conventional static security constrained OPF programs to include consideration of the dynamic security level of the on-line states. A dynamic security monitor and a preventive control module are introduced to form a complete static and dynamic security constrained OPF scheme. The concept of security in power system operation is expanded to include dynamic contingency prevention that could lead to a complete system collapse. It is envisaged that the incorporation of the transient security dispatch would contribute to improving operational security with due consideration of economy of operation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power transfer control and generation rescheduling in emergencies
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: A method of emergency control which considers load-shedding and overload control is proposed. The inclusion of frequency falls occurring simultaneously with overloads is used for the analysis. System overload concept is used for computer definition of generation rescheduling and interarea power transfers. Results of simulation in a small sample system show good response in interarea power transfer partial recovery and frequency improvement. This effect may be helpful in a reduction of load-shedding in some instances with the consequent improvement of the security of service during emergencies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Specification of high resolution graphics man/machine interface for British Rail's electric traction power supply network SCADA systems
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: Control of electric traction power supply networks associated with electrified railways has been a requirement in Britain since the turn of this century. The first electrification schemes lacked remote control facilities, each large sub-station site being manned. The author looks at the gradual introduction of high resolution graphics man/machine interfaces in the control rooms with SCADA systems. The involvement of the operators in the design of the system is also described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Prediction models for the incremental cost and the water worth functions based on hydro-thermal OPF
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: A hydro-thermal electric power system is considered. The object is to find the active power generation schedule to meet a predicted active and reactive power demand profile and simultaneously achieve maximum economy. The scheduling is planned for an appropriate time interval. The problem is commonly known as the hydro-thermal optimal power flow.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Standard master for regional telecontrol (SMART) for distribution networks
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The author discusses the planned implementation of computer based telecontrol master stations for use in the distribution regions of Eskom, the electricity utility of South Africa. The requirements for and the philosophy behind this project, known as SMART, are given and the advantages and disadvantages of the standardised approach are highlighted. The conclusions drawn from the analysis of the benefits of the standardised approach proved that there are major financial and technical advantages for Eskom.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: System design aspects of an advanced despatcher training simulator
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The increasing complexity of power system operation the need for efficient operational planning/analysis tools and the requirement for quality training of new staff within reduced time scales have promoted the need for advanced despatcher training simulators. The authors outline a despatcher training simulator (DTS) system implemented by Westinghouse Systems Limited. The DTS system is based on standard products of ESCA Corporation of Bellevue, USA and standard products from Westinghouse Systems Limited. The DTS design, which uses a client-server approach for information exchange between subsystems is described. The implementation aspects on total energy control system projects on incremental projects and on stand alone implementations are considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Daily load curve forecasting via automatic selection of models
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: A daily load curve forecasting method is proposed. In the method, the best load model is selected automatically based on a criterion, and the special days effect on the load is classified and modelled. Thus the authors can treat the time varying nature of the load and special days effect in a suitable and effective way. There exist various kinds of factors which have influences on the load but not included in the models here, e.g., weather, humidity and economic situation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A best-first strategy for voltage and reactive power control
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The authors present an expert system based on a modified best-first search strategy, which assists the power system planning operator in voltage control and reactive power dispatching. An experimental PROLOG program, based on the proposed strategy, is developed. Tests on several study systems show promising results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Applications of micro computer database software to power systems monitoring problems
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The authors report on the applications of a well established database management system to data manipulation, presentation, revisions and updates. The database relates to both grid and primary substation, weekly demand information, system daily load information for short-term forecasting objectives, statistical faults report for reliability evaluation of power systems, generation and transmission data for system performance studies. Additional provision is made to include substation equipment inventory data to aid network reinforcement planning objectives.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integration of the optimal power flow into generation control and dispatch
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: A close interaction of automatic generation control (AGC), reserve monitor (RM), and economic dispatch (ED) is prerequisite of economic and reliable operation. In power systems where network limitations frequently constrain pure economic dispatch an integration of optimal power flow (OPF) is necessary. The primary practical requirements are best met by applying a general purpose OPF package using a full AC network model and unit models originating from the generation control and dispatch subsystem, including piecewise quadratic cost curves. The authors describe a closed-loop OPF based on a general-purpose, nonspecialized OPF package. All functions described form an integrated part of an EMS package.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive control with multistep predictor for power system load frequency
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: A design method for a load frequency adaptive controller is presented considering the time-delay. Using the recursive extended least squares method combined with the F-testing method, a new strategy of identifying the CARMA model for load frequency control is developed. An adaptive controller with multistep predictor is designed. The control effects are validated on a simulation system. The computer result is encouraging.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fuzzy coordination of economy, security and quality in power system generation control
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: In the operation of power systems it has become necessary not only to consider pursuit of economy but also to take various other requirements into consideration. In order to do away with the shortcomings of conventional approaches, a technique determining the optimal operation states has been proposed, whereby operating problems involving plural objectives are formulated as multi-objective programming, and the fuzzy coordination technique is applied. Economy has been selected as the primary objective while security and the ensuring of AFC (automatic frequency control) regulation capacity have been taken up as sub-objectives. While the pursuit of economy is indispensable to supply low-priced electric power to the customers, consideration for security should be conducted in order to provide stable electric power supply. A new evolution index for AFC regulation capacity margin is proposed. The effectiveness of the technique ensuring AFC regulation capacity margin based on the fuzzy coordination technique with consideration given to economy and security is clarified.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An advanced system for energy management in Helsinki
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The authors describe the philosophy and implementation of managing the electric and district heating energy supply in Helsinki. The structure of the networks and their interdependence is described as well as the control strategy, handled by a central control system and separate district centres for the electric and district heating networks. The authors emphasise the main control centre with its connections to district centres, neighbouring utility control centres, weather forecast system, energy data collection system, PC-network for statistical calculations and long term planning activities, expert system applications etc. The following forecast and planning applications and their use in real-time as well as in an advanced planning environment of the main control centre are described. Advanced network calculation functions for the electrical and district heating networks in both real-time and in planning mode are also described. The operational and economic benefits of the system are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integration and coordination of power system control and protection
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The authors review the subject of integrated microprocessor based systems capable of carrying out the control and protection functions currently undertaken in substations, together with possible additional functions that are being designed to assist in the better management of power systems as a whole.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Upgrading Ireland's National Control Centre
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The authors describe the control system which is in operation in the National Control Centre, Ireland. Its limitations, together with the other reasons which prompted the upgrade are described. The underlying reasons for the Electricity Supply Board's commitment to a distributed computing architecture in order to avoid the hardware constraints experienced with the original system are outlined. The architecture of the new system, in terms of hardware, SCADA functions and power application software is discussed. The management of the project, together with the critical milestones and planned switch-over are also described. Future plans for items such as closed-loop load frequency control, optimal power flow and a dispatcher training simulator are itemised.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integrated substation control and protection-a co-ordinated protection approach
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: A new generation of protection schemes for application to the Eskom electrical network is currently being introduced into the organization. The new protection schemes focus on two key aspects, namely a technological move to the use of microprocessor-based equipment, and an approach which facilitates the co-ordination of the protection with an integrated control system. The author describes Eskom's approach to the introduction of the new generation of protection schemes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An advanced package for management of distribution system operations
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The authors provide an overview of an operations management system by Westinghouse Systems Limited for the power distribution industry. System requirements together with the main features of design and the aspects of system software pertinent to the operation of distribution networks are covered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Potential advantages of a diagnostic expert system for assisting operator response to system events
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The fault diagnosis expert system, RESPONDD, has been presented as a useful tool in helping operators diagnose system faults, assisting the fulfilment of their other duties, and helping attain a high standard in trainees. The areas in which assistance is given include operating under emergency conditions, restoring supply, restoring plant, routine maintenance and accounting for protection behaviour. Thereby major benefits in the operation of a power system are attainable. More so with continuing developments in control centre and substation equipment which shall continue to increase the large levels of SCADA data available. The potential for increased awareness of system conditions will only be attained if help is given to diagnose the incoming data and subsequently respond appropriately-such an expert system could fulfil this role.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementation of a low cost rural telecontrol and monitoring system
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The village of Sevenoaks Weald in Kent lies to the south of the major town of Sevenoaks supplied by a long overhead line feeder. The long feeder has a history of problems and Seeboard was concerned to improve the performance of the supply network for the customers in the village. Air break isolating switches are to be used on the line and the authors look at a prototype communication and control system for them.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distributed design for energy management systems
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: Host based designs have become a serious bottleneck in energy management systems (EMS). Functional requirements will continue to grow much faster than throughput in host based systems resulting in deteriorating response times and performance. The new distributed design based on open system architecture is the solution for this problem and will be the platform for a new era in power system control.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Extending SCADA systems to provide cost effective distribution switchgear condition monitoring
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The authors describe the design and application of a microprocessor controlled disturbance recorder (MCDR) which can be interfaced to the remote terminal unit (RTU) of a SCADA system. The recorder stores the instantaneous voltage and current values, and status of the circuit breaker auxiliary contacts, at a rate sufficient to allow it to perform a post-fault computation of the amplitude and duration of the arc current(s) in each phase of the circuit breaker. These computed values are then communicated to the RTU from where they can be accessed by the central hardware of the SCADA network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new alarm processing for the forthcoming national control system of Electricite de France
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: Taking advantage of the improvements made in computer tools. Electricite de France is undertaking the overall renovation of its power control centers in order to optimize the operation of the generation-transmission system from the savings and security point of view. The alarm processing function has been set into a consistent whole with different synthesis levels in order to show the operator only the significant events. This process has needed an ergonomic analysis of operator activity. From the results of this analysis the authors defined the processing operations to assist the operator in understanding the situation and when possible to aid functions for decision making.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Requirements for a load forecasting system in the privatised supply industry
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The authors define the functions which are supported in an electrical load forecasting system. They show how existing algorithms and techniques have been integrated into a comprehensive product, which includes a supporting database and graphics-based human computer interface. This product is aimed at the specific needs of the industry and may be regarded as a first step towards a total energy management facility.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: MORGAT: A tool for electric transient simulation. An application to the restoration of a power system after a major failure
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: After a major power system failure, the first stages of the restoration process are very critical because of the transient phenomena which may arise and cause damage to the equipment. In order to design restoration procedures taking these risks into account, Electricite de France has been led to use MORGAT, a tool initially designed for relay tests. Some results gained from simulation are given and compared with on-site results. They show that MORGAT is a suitable tool for the study of transient phenomena occurring during the first re-energizing procedures of the restoration plan.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A fully integrated computer-based system for distribution control room operations
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The system described will soon go into operational use as the primary means for control of Eastern Electricity's 132 kV, 33 kV and 11 kV distribution network. Control will normally be exercised from a single large control centre but can also be effected from a small emergency control centre. Sections 2 and 3 outline Eastern Electricity's distribution business and the preparations which were made for procurement of the new system. The system itself is described in Section 4. Section 5 discusses the initial level of system integration, and plans for further integration are outlined in Section 6. Present conclusions are noted in Section 7.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dispatch of spinning reserve
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: Maintaining system frequency within operational and statutory limits following generation infeed losses requires sufficient active power reserves. An enhanced dispatch algorithm is presented in which generator loading and operating pressure are instructed to provide spinning reserve in the most economical way. A power system simulation is also presented to illustrate the benefits of adopting such an algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The determination of the cost savings in economic dispatch calculations by improving the accuracy of the input data
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The economic dispatch problem is considered. In online applications, the optimality of the results obtained from these economic dispatch calculations depends on the inaccuracies of the input data, e.g. on the inaccuracies of the incremental cost curves, of the line impedances, of the transformer turns ratios, etc. A proposal is made for the determination of the cost savings when the accuracy of this input data is improved.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distribution management system-implementation of an integrated approach
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: Southern Electric, in conjunction with Westinghouse Systems Ltd, has commenced the development of a distribution management system. This joint project, known as COMAND, Control Management and Network Display system, draws on the user skills and specialist knowledge of Southern Electric and combines it with the real-time systems expertise of WSL to produce an optimum solution to a computer-based control room information system. The authors describe the implementation of the COMAND system to achieve maximum flexibility for the control function by establishing a corporate approach to the handling of data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new centre for national control-an evolutionary transition
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: Control of the National Grid Company (NGC) power system, and of generators of dispatchable size, is effected currently through a National Control Centre (NCC) in London, and 6 Area Control Centres (ACCs), at Leeds, Manchester, Birmingham, St. Albans, East Grinstead and Bristol. This arrangement is hierarchical, NCC occupying the tier responsible for overall control of the NGC system and for co-ordination of ACC activities, and ACCs the tier responsible for detailed control implementation. These control functions are discharged by Grid System Management (GSM). In December 1988, the Central Electricity Generating Board, placed a contract with Control Data Corporation of Minneapolis, to supply energy management systems (EMS) for one NCC and four ACCs. This enterprise is known as the Five Centre Grid Control Project, now vested with NGC and is due for commissioning in 1993 at all five Control Centres. Upon commissioning, merging of Manchester with Leeds, and East Grinstead with St. Albans ACCs will take place. The authors discuss evolution of the EMS user specification and design, in terms of facilities to be provided at the new NCC.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automatic control of voltage instability by an expert system utilizing pattern recognition techniques
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Power System Monitoring and Control
abstract: The authors describe a knowledge-based algorithm for automatic control of extreme disturbances that could lead to system voltage instability. The study results show that it could adapt for quite different types of disturbance-be it loss of lines or loss of generation-to sustain system voltage stability. A new methodology has been developed that utilises the pattern recognition method in the areas of reactive power control following a contingency. Based on this new methodology, the operators can be provided with a priority list for searching the best available control measures after each contingency. The consequence of each chosen control measure can be predicted beforehand. The algorithm makes use of the knowledge about the system, sensitive factors, operating rules, operator's experience and other requirements for good system operation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
